narration.full_text: Now that we've covered the basic trigonometric ratios, let's introduce their reciprocals. These are cosecant, secant, and cotangent, and they are simply the inverse of sine, cosine, and tangent, respectively. Understanding these reciprocal identities is crucial for solving more complex trigonometric problems. First, the cosecant of an angle, often written as csc, is the reciprocal of the sine of that angle. So, if sine is opposite over hypotenuse, then cosecant is hypotenuse over opposite. Next, the secant of an angle, denoted as sec, is the reciprocal of the cosine of that angle. Since cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse, secant becomes hypotenuse over adjacent. Finally, the cotangent of an angle, or cot, is the reciprocal of the tangent. If tangent is opposite over adjacent, then cotangent is adjacent over opposite. These relationships allow us to express any of the six trigonometric ratios in terms of the others, simplifying calculations and proofs. Keep these reciprocal identities in mind as we continue to explore trigonometry.
